narrative.title: The Gate Reader That Must Not Duplicate Memory
narrative.scenario: A secure gate reads a one-way access chain and must confirm the code is a palindrome before opening — but the controller is too small to hold a second copy of the code. The trick: split the chain at its middle, flip the rear half in place, and then compare the two halves node by node as they march in lockstep.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of node values representing the linked list.
narrative.outputFormat: true when the list reads the same forwards and backwards, false otherwise.

testCases.explanation: Front half 1-2 matches the flipped rear half 2-1 station for station.
The halves disagree at the very first comparison.

hintLevels: Level 1: A palindrome is two mirror halves — find the middle and compare outward-inward.
Level 2: Slow/fast pointers find the middle, reverse everything from there, then walk both halves together checking values.

Level 3: Reversing the rear half (not the front) lets the front pointer simply walk to the middle while the flipped half walks to meet it; odd-length tails compare harmlessly because the flipped half is the shorter one.
